articles.title: After losing their home in Gaza, a Palestinian potter turned clay into dome-shaped shelter for his parents as shortages of cement and steel stall reconstruction
articles.summary: After spending two years living in a tent, Palestinian potter Jaafar Atallah decided to turn the very earth beneath his feet into a home for his parents.
articles.body: After spending two years living in a tent, Palestinian potter Jaafar Atallah decided to turn the very earth beneath his feet into a home for his parents. With cement and steel difficult to obtain in Gaza, he gathered around 15 people, collected local clay and experimented with mud bricks until they managed to build a dome-shaped dwelling. The Financial Times reported on Atallah’s effort in June 2026, describing how his family’s traditional pottery skills had become a way to seek shelter amid widespread destruction and shortages of construction materials.For Atallah, the project was about more than building walls. It was an attempt to give his parents a measure of protection and dignity after their home was destroyed during the war. The dome drew on a familiar shape from his family’s pottery tradition: the bread ovens they had made for generations. This time, however, the structure was large enough for people to live in.From pottery to building homesAtallah had earned his living making bowls, vases and other pottery items using clay found near his home in northern Gaza. The war destroyed the family’s home and pottery factory, forcing them to relocate and rebuild their lives elsewhere in the territory.After enduring life in a tent, he began exploring whether the same material used in his craft could help create a more substantial shelter. With help from family members and other workers, including his father, who was also a potter, he collected clay and shaped it into bricks. The process was not straightforward. The team experimented with different mixtures and tested several prototypes before finding a combination that could hold together. The mixture included clay, water, ash and powdered glass. Atallah also developed a waterproof glaze for the bricks, attempting to make the structure more resistant to the elements.The result was a domed clay dwelling that the team described as strong enough for a person to stand on top of it. The construction offered an alternative to the fragile tents in which many displaced Palestinians continue to live.Atallah explained the practical difference in an interview with the Financial Times, saying that food could be stored in the clay structure, unlike in a tent where fresh produce could spoil quickly in the summer heat. He described the heat inside tents as torture, underscoring how extreme weather compounds the hardship of displacement.A housing crisis with few alternativesAtallah’s initiative comes amid a severe housing crisis in Gaza, where years of bombardment have damaged or destroyed homes, public infrastructure and businesses. The Financial Times and Asharq Al-Awsat reported that shortages of essential construction materials, including cement and steel, have pushed residents towards improvised methods of repairing or rebuilding shelters.According to UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs, Israel has restricted the entry of construction materials into Gaza, calling them 'dual-use' mateirals and citing concerns that items such as cement and steel could be diverted by Hamas for military purposes, including tunnel construction. The restrictions have left residents and humanitarian organisations struggling to find materials for reconstruction. Israeli authorities’ security rationale and the consequences for civilian housing are central to the wider dispute over rebuilding the territory.According to figures cited in the Financial Times report from the United Nations, around 1.9 million people in Gaza were displaced or living in tents. Many shelters lack adequate sanitation and basic utilities, leaving families exposed to heat, cold and flooding. With conventional construction materials scarce, residents have turned to whatever they can recover locally. Some collect stones and concrete fragments from destroyed buildings, while others reuse steel reinforcement bars or make mud-based mortar. These approaches may help protect a tent or repair a damaged wall, but they are not a substitute for a comprehensive reconstruction effort.The Norwegian Refugee Council’s Gaza shelter coordinator, Iyad Abu Hamam, cautioned that recycled concrete does not achieve the strength required for many building applications. The improvised use of rubble and mud therefore has significant limits, particularly when it comes to roofs and structures that must meet safety standards.Turning rubble into a resourceAtallah is not the only Gazan trying to find building materials in the remains of destroyed homes. Teenage sisters Tala and Farah Moussa have been experimenting with bricks made from crushed concrete debris, mud, ash and powdered glass.Their idea emerged after their own house was bombed. The sisters, who had been displaced multiple times with their family, began crushing concrete into smaller pieces and testing different mixtures to make usable blocks. After five or six prototypes, they developed a mixture suitable for applications such as pavements and partitions.In May 2026, the sisters won a youth innovation award from the Swiss-based Earth Foundation, receiving $12,500 that they hoped to use to organise workshops and teach others their technique, according to the Financial Times and Asharq Al-Awsat.Their work reflects a broader effort to reuse materials that would otherwise remain part of Gaza's enormous rubble piles. However, the sisters' bricks and Atallah's clay structures should not be mistaken for fully tested replacements for conventional construction materials.Builders have also salvaged steel reinforcement bars from destroyed buildings, although corrosion can limit their usefulness. Others have collected cement that reportedly surfaced in the Maghazi area after Israeli forces pumped material into a tunnel to seal it.Sharing a possible way forwardAtallah's project has attracted attention beyond his immediate community. After he shared videos of the construction process online, pottery groups around the world offered support. The videos also helped spread the idea that locally available clay could be used to create shelters when conventional supplies were unavailable.Khalil Abu Ramadan, a social media personality known for making clay sculptures, documented the construction and helped promote the approach. Atallah subsequently began working on another clay home for himself and his wife.The aim is to encourage other families to explore similar methods. For people living in tents, the prospect of a more substantial shelter is compelling, particularly when temporary accommodation offers little protection from extreme temperatures or other hazards.Yet building with locally available materials is not necessarily inexpensive. Even clay, rubble and other resources can involve considerable labour and costs in Gaza's wartime economy. Nor does a dome's apparent strength establish that it can withstand every structural or weather-related risk.Hope amid the destructionAs per a New York Times report, efforts such as Atallah's within a broader picture of Palestinians attempting to rebuild their lives. Even after a ceasefire agreement, residents have continued to face destruction, displacement and uncertainty. Families are trying to restore livelihoods, children are attending makeshift classrooms, and communities are searching for ways to reclaim everyday routines.The clay homes represent one small part of that struggle. They cannot replace the scale of reconstruction required across Gaza, but they demonstrate how traditional skills and locally available materials can be adapted to meet urgent needs.For Atallah, pottery has taken on a different purpose. The clay that once supplied his family's livelihood is now being used to create shelter for those who lost their home. His work offers a glimpse of what rebuilding can look like when families cannot wait for conventional supplies to become available.The larger challenge remains unresolved: improvised homes can provide some relief, but lasting recovery will require safe access to construction materials, adequate infrastructure, technical expertise and the resources needed to rebuild damaged communities.You use AI every day. articles.title: Austrian Airlines finds no threat after bomb alert diverts Tel Aviv-Vienna flight to Sofia
articles.summary: Austrian Airlines said on Monday that searches of the aircraft operating flight OS82, along with its passengers and crew, in Sofia revealed no threat
articles.body: Austrian Airlines said on Monday that searches of the aircraft operating flight OS82, along with its passengers and crew, in Sofia revealed no threat after a security alert forced the Tel Aviv–Vienna flight to divert on Sunday.The airline said the aircraft, carrying 51 passengers and six crew members, resumed its journey to Vienna from Sofia later that night, with all passengers remaining on board, according to the news agency Reuters.Earlier, an Austrian airlines flight travelling from Tel Aviv to Vienna made an emergency landing in Sofia, Bulgaria, after its crew reported a bomb threat during the journey, prompting a security operation.The Airbus A320, operating as flight OS82, was diverted to Sofia after the threat was reported near the Romanian border, according to Bulgaria’s Ministry of Transport and Communications. All passengers were evacuated after the aircraft landed.A Bulgarian Air Force fighter jet was also scrambled and escorted the aircraft until it reached Sofia airport, the ministry added. Authorities subsequently set up a crisis management headquarters and began inspecting the plane.Anonymous bomb report triggers security alertAccording to Israeli news outlet Ynet, passengers said the diversion followed an anonymous report alleging that a bomb was on board. The Times of Israel also reported that security concerns emerged after a suspicious object was allegedly spotted on the aircraft’s deck. The plane reportedly transmitted an emergency signal.The aircraft was carrying a delegation of young people scheduled to speak at the United Nations, The Times of Israel reported.The incident comes less than three weeks after a security scare involving a Flydubai flight bound for Tel Aviv.You use AI every day. articles.title: Indian-origin couple invested over $100,000 of their life savings into opening their dream vegan cafe in Australia; an arson attack against tobacconists has left them raising funds for repairs
articles.summary: Ashish Sharma and Manali Purohit had invested almost all of their life savings into opening their dream vegan cafe in Melbourne.
articles.body: Ashish Sharma and Manali Purohit had invested almost all of their life savings into opening their dream vegan cafe in Melbourne. But after just three months of operating, they lost their entire space to an arson attack by tobacconists, as per a report by The Australia Today.On the morning of October 12, the cafe was severely damaged in a suspected arson attack that gutted the tobacco shop next door, which had opened in recent weeks. The day after the firebombing, about $5,000 worth of technology and equipment was stolen from the burnt-out cafe. When the couple entered the cafe after the robbery, Sharma said it felt like their "dream had been ripped away." “It felt like a warzone,” he said. “The roof had melted off – soot everywhere.”It was in July 2026 that the couple's cafe 'And Bodega' opened in Melbourne's Fitzroy North. The name was a nod to the neighbourhood convenience stores synonymous with New York. They had spent the past five months scouring Facebook Marketplace for second-hand furniture, layered coats of paint on walls and installed plumbing to fit out their dream. “We put in basically all our life savings. We did a lot of it DIY,” said co-owner Sharma to The Guardian. Purohit, who grew up in Mumbai and trained as a pastry chef in India, had hoped their plant-based cafe would become a welcoming neighbourhood destination.When a new business moved in next door, they initially believed it would be a grocery store that complemented their cafe. However, their concerns grew when they realised it may be a tobacco shop instead. The couple said customers had also expressed fears about the possibility of arson attacks, amid a wider wave of firebombings targeting tobacconists across Victoria. This attack has come amid a series of firebombings attacking tobacconists across Melbourne, with hundreds hit since late 2023.In late September, Purohit noticed broken glass at the neighbouring shop and a handwritten note on its wall. The tobacconist’s windows were reportedly smashed again shortly before the October attack.Emergency services were called to respond to reports of an explosion on St Georges Road about 3:40 am on Monday. Police investigators believe one or multiple offenders forced entry into the tobacco shop and set it alight. The tobacconist was completely destroyed, while And Bodega and other neighbouring businesses were damaged, police said in a statement.According to Guardian Australia, small businesses located near tobacconists are being denied insurance or priced out of coverage as rising arson attacks lead to collateral damage. For Sharma and Purohit, their contents insurance, taken out before the tobacco store opening, is expected to provide a payout of about $25,000. But the funds are not expected to cover the costs of rebuilding the cafe at the same location.Currently, the couple have set up a crowdfunding campaign to raise funds for repairing and replacing equipment, paying outstanding staff and supplier costs while looking for a new home for And Bodega. “The only reason we’re positive is because of the people,” Sharma said. “It’s really overwhelming, the love and support.”Purohit said they have also received offers from fellow small businesses to donate portions of their profits to the couple, host fundraisers and drop off ice-cream. “Words can’t describe just how seen and loved we feel,” she said.In September 2026, new laws allowing inspectors to close stores that sell illegal tobacco products came into effect in Victoria. However, the Victorian Coalition said the government's new closure powers "had barely made a dent" and vowed that if elected next month, it would bolster laws and increase police presence to close down illegal retailers.As for Sharma and Purohit, they hope to reopen And Bodega as a smaller hole-in-the-wall cafe serving baked goods and coffee. “If we can restart, it’s at least one small way to fight against the violence,” Sharma said.You use AI every day. articles.title: At 14, Oregon teenager Elijah Buckwald climbed onto an overturned pickup to help free an elderly couple trapped inside; two years later, at 16, he received Scouting America’s Honor Medal for lifesaving heroism
articles.summary: Some moments leave little time for hesitation.
articles.body: Some moments leave little time for hesitation. For Elijah Buckwald, a routine drive through Oregon’s Santiam Pass became one of those moments when, at just 14, he found himself standing on an overturned pickup truck, helping strangers trapped inside after a serious crash. Two years later, that instinct to step forward has earned the Redmond teenager national recognition, states an online report by KTVZ21 News.A crash on Santiam PassAccording to the report, in August 2024, Buckwald was travelling with his grandparents near the summit of Santiam Pass when they encountered an overturned pickup truck and camper trailer blocking the highway. Inside the wreckage was an elderly couple who needed help.With emergency responders yet to arrive, Buckwald got out to assess the situation. He climbed onto the overturned pickup, reached the passenger side and opened the door. He then held it in place while other adults worked to get the couple safely out of the vehicle.The quick response helped create an opening for the trapped occupants to be brought to safety. Despite the severity of the crash, neither person was injured.For Buckwald, who was only 14 at the time, the situation called for action rather than waiting for someone else to take charge, adds the online report.Recognition for a lifesaving actNow 16 and a member of Scout Troop 25, Buckwald has been recognised with Scouting America’s prestigious Honor Medal, a national award presented to Scouts and adult leaders for acts of heroism and lifesaving service, also adds the report.The honour places his actions on Santiam Pass among the organisation’s recognised examples of courage and preparedness. It also highlights how skills developed through Scouting can become valuable in unexpected, real-world emergencies.Buckwald’s actions were carried out before professional first responders reached the scene, making his willingness to help particularly significant, informs the report too.When training meets instinctThe incident has also become a point of pride for Buckwald’s troop, where preparedness and service are central parts of the Scouting experience. His actions demonstrated how training can translate into calm decision-making when circumstances suddenly become dangerous.What began as an ordinary journey with his grandparents ultimately became a defining moment for the teenager. At an age when most people might have stood back and waited for help, Buckwald moved towards the overturned vehicle and helped make a dangerous situation safer.His recognition two years later serves as a reminder that heroism does not always arrive with dramatic gestures.Images Courtesy: Facebook and KTVZ21 NewsYou use AI every day. articles.title: 2 killed, 3 hurt in late-night shooting at Baltimore gas station in US
articles.summary: A man and a woman were killed and three other people injured in a shooting at a gas station in West Baltimore in US on Sunday night, police said.
articles.body: A man and a woman were killed and three other people injured in a shooting at a gas station in West Baltimore in US on Sunday night, police said.Officers were called to the BP gas station in the 2800 block of Edmondson Avenue at around 10.30 pm. They found four people — a woman and three men — suffering from gunshot wounds. A fifth victim, a man, later arrived at a hospital with similar injuries, according to the CBS News.Baltimore police commissioner Richard Worley confirmed that the woman and one of the men had died. The remaining three victims were expected to survive.Investigators are still trying to establish the motive behind the shooting, Worley said.“We don't know any of that yet,” he said, adding that investigators hoped to obtain information by speaking to the surviving victims. He noted that police often rely on video footage to piece together what happened.According to Worley, two or three gunmen may have been involved, and high-powered rifles were used in the attack. No arrests had been made as of Sunday night.Baltimore grapples with recent mass shootingsThe latest incident comes amid a series of shootings in Baltimore over the past month. Police have responded to at least four mass shootings during this period, including an attack earlier this month that killed a 12-year-old at a park in West Baltimore.Another shooting in the city's Winchester neighbourhood left an 18-year-old and a 19-year-old dead.Worley expressed frustration over what he described as young people firing weapons indiscriminately without knowing how to handle or control them, resulting in multiple people being shot.He said police would continue working to solve the latest case and hold those responsible for the two deaths accountable.Anyone with information about the gas station shooting has been asked to contact Baltimore police at 410-396-2466 or Metro Crime Stoppers at 1-866-7LOCKUP.Separate shooting at liquor store injures threeEarlier on Sunday evening, three people were wounded in a separate shooting at a liquor store in northwest Baltimore, police said.Officers arrived at Pepper Liquor Store in the 5400 block of Reisterstown Road at around 8.30 pm, where they found two women, aged 26 and 22, suffering from gunshot wounds. Both were taken to a hospital in stable condition.While officers were at the scene, they learnt that a 27-year-old man had also arrived at a hospital with gunshot wounds that were not considered life-threatening.Police have urged anyone with information about the liquor store shooting to call 410-396-2466 or contact Metro Crime Stoppers at 1-866-7LOCKUP.You use AI every day. articles.title: ‘We will all die one day’: Ecuador priest killed by falling crucifix moments after sermon
articles.summary: Moments after preaching about life’s fleeting nature and the importance of faith and family, a Roman Catholic priest in Ecuador was killed when a heavy
articles.body: Moments after preaching about life’s fleeting nature and the importance of faith and family, a Roman Catholic priest in Ecuador was killed when a heavy crucifix fell on his head during a livestreamed Mass.Father Patricio Alfredo Sánchez Molinari died on Saturday at the Church of Perpetual Relief in Guayaquil, a coastal city in southwestern Ecuador, around 265 km from the capital, Quito. The Archdiocese of Guayaquil identified him as the parish priest of the church.According to footage reviewed by NBC News and described by The Independent, the large crucifix mounted on the wall behind the altar suddenly detached and fell forward, striking the back of the priest’s head. Sánchez was facing the congregation and appeared not to notice the crucifix falling behind him.The livestream captured worshippers rushing to help as cries for assistance were heard. “Father, Father! Call an ambulance!” people could be heard shouting, according to The Independent. The broadcast continued briefly before cutting out. The video was subsequently taken down.Emergency services were called to the scene, but first responders were unable to revive the priest. Local authorities had not publicly commented on the incident in the reports available.Priest reflected on life before the accidentThe New York Post reported that during his sermon, he urged worshippers not to spend their lives scrolling on their phones, but to devote time to God and their loved ones.“One day, all of us here will also die, and sometimes the time we’ve spent on things doesn’t have as much meaning as the time we spend with God,” he said.He also spoke about the importance of relationships and faith, adding, “The quality time we give to God, to our brothers and sisters, to our husbands, wives, children, and family— that time is the best spent."The priest was beginning another prayer and asking God to bless the congregation when the crucifix fell, the newspaper reported.The Archdiocese of Guayaquil announced Sánchez’s death in a statement, saying he “has left to the House of the Father to enjoy his presence and glory”.Sánchez belonged to the Congregation of the Most Holy Redeemer, a Roman Catholic religious order founded in 1732 with a presence in 80 countries.You use AI every day. articles.title: ‘Worried about his future, saddened by 3 deaths’: Mother of accused in Kochi Mini Cooper crash
articles.summary: KOCHI: Nooha, mother of Suhail, the prime accused in the Mini Cooper crash that killed three youngsters at Nedumbassery, has expressed solidarity with the
articles.body: KOCHI: Nooha, mother of Suhail, the prime accused in the Mini Cooper crash that killed three youngsters at Nedumbassery, has expressed solidarity with the victims' families, saying she understands their grief and that her family will stand by them.In a video posted on the Instagram page of Iha Design, which she owns, Nooha offered condolences to the bereaved families and said the loss of a child was a pain beyond imagination."When we raise our children with so much love, watch them grow up and look forward to their dreams and future, losing them midway is a pain beyond what we can even imagine. I understand that," she said."I am someone who understands the pain a mother or father goes through when they lose a child. I know that none of my words can lessen the immense grief the families are experiencing," she said.Nooha said she and her family would support the victims' families during their time of grief."As a mother and as a member of society, I want to express my support for the family of the three youngsters. My family and I stand by them. As long as we are here, we will continue to support that family," she said.She clarified that her statement was not intended to minimise or compare anyone's suffering, but to express her own helplessness.On the investigation, Nooha said the authorities should be allowed to proceed fairly and establish the truth."Let the investigation take its course and let the law proceed in accordance with the law. I only wish that everything is handled fairly and that only the truth comes out," she said.With the incident being widely discussed on social media, she also appealed to people to show compassion and respect her family's privacy. She said her family comprised four members and urged people not to circulate baseless reports about them."On one side, I am worried about my child's future and what lies ahead for him. At the same time, I am deeply saddened by the loss of the lives of those three youngsters. I do not know how to deal with both these emotions or what I should say or do," she said.MVD issues show-cause notice to SuhailMeanwhile, the Motor Vehicles Department (MVD) has issued a show-cause notice to Suhail as part of proceedings to suspend or cancel his driving licence, officials said on Sunday.The notice was issued by the Ernakulam Regional Transport Officer (RTO) following a recommendation from the police investigating the accident. Suhail has been asked to respond within 14 days, after which the department will decide on further action, officials said.MVD officials said they had received a detailed police report recommending cancellation of his licence. Police also found that the Mini Cooper's exhaust system had allegedly been modified, causing excessive noise.Suhail, 19, was allegedly driving the car when it rammed into a scooter carrying three youngsters on the airport road at Nedumbassery in the early hours of October 11. The three victims, including two women, were around 21 years old.Police have also arrested Ninav, Ameer and Joel, who were in the car at the time of the crash.Police cite alcohol levels and speed in bail oppositionIn a report submitted to the Angamaly Judicial First Class Magistrate Court while opposing Suhail's bail plea, police said his blood sample recorded an alcohol concentration of 161 mg per 100 ml, while his urine sample showed 230 mg per 100 ml.The reported blood alcohol concentration was substantially above the permissible limit of 30 mg per 100 ml under Section 185 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988.According to the police report, Suhail allegedly drove at more than 100 kmph on a public road while heavily intoxicated, with the other accused accompanying him. The permissible speed limit on the stretch was 60 or 70 kmph, the report said.A court on Saturday dismissed the bail petitions of all four accused.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Kochi | Silver Rate in Kochi | Bank Holidays in Kochi | Public Holidays in KochiStay updated with the latest Kochi news. articles.summary: Russia’s finance minister Anton Siluanov will also serve as a deputy prime minister following a cabinet reshuffle approved by President Vladimir Putin on
articles.body: Russia’s finance minister Anton Siluanov will also serve as a deputy prime minister following a cabinet reshuffle approved by President Vladimir Putin on Monday, news agency Reuters reported.Vladimir Putin approved major changes to the country’s top government positions weeks after the ruling United Russia party secured its largest-ever majority in parliamentary elections.The reshuffle affects nearly half of PM Mikhail Mishustin’s deputy prime ministers.One of the key changes is the removal of Dmitry Grigorenko as chief of government staff.According to The Moscow Times, Rustamova said the move was unexpected, given Grigorenko’s close working relationship with Mishustin and his important role in the government.Siluanov, who has served as finance minister since 2011, will continue in that role while taking on additional responsibilities as deputy prime minister.He previously held both positions from 2018 to 2020 under former Prime Minister Dmitry Medvedev.Transportation minister Andrei Nikitin will also become a deputy prime minister, overseeing the development of Russia’s transportation sector, among other responsibilities.The post became vacant after Vitaly Savelyev resigned following his election to the lower house of parliament, the State Duma, in late September.You use AI every day. articles.title: Army officer's Nissan car broke down after waterlogging and repairs in 2021; now, Delhi consumer commission orders service centre to repair it for free and pay Rs 50,000
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: A consumer commission in Delhi has held a car service centre guilty of deficiency in service after it failed to properly repair a Nissan car
articles.body: NEW DELHI: A consumer commission in Delhi has held a car service centre guilty of deficiency in service after it failed to properly repair a Nissan car that had been partially submerged in waterlogging, with the vehicle developing a gearbox problem within a month of being returned to its owner after repairs.The District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission, South-West Delhi, directed Youwe and Cars, the car’s authorised service centre, to repair the vehicle free of cost and pay Rs 50,000 as compensation for mental harassment, agony and litigation expenses, in its order dated October 6, 2026.Nissan car repair disputeAccording to the commission order, the complainant, a serving Army officer, purchased the car on April 9, 2019, and insured it with ICICI Lombard in June 2021. On July 28, 2021, the vehicle was partially submerged due to waterlogging in a parking lot in Vasant Kunj, Delhi.The car was towed to Youwe and Cars for repairs. The service centre initially estimated the repair cost at Rs 6,79,092, which was later reduced to Rs 4,21,000 and then to Rs 3,61,403. The complainant alleged that the service centre did not explain the reduction in the estimate or obtain her consent before replacing consumables and parts not covered by the insurance policy.She took delivery of the car on January 21, 2022, but alleged that the steering module made a noise, the Nissan Connect module was not working and some parts had not been replaced. The car broke down the same day and developed another problem on February 9, 2022, when it became immobile near Dhaula Kuan. It was towed back to the service centre, where it remained.The complainant alleged that the service centre had failed to properly repair the car and address the gearbox damage. She issued a legal notice to the opposite parties on March 16, 2022, before approaching the commission.Youwe and Cars and Nissan Motor India did not file their replies within the prescribed period and were proceeded against ex parte. ICICI Lombard denied deficiency in service, stating that it had paid Rs 3,40,263 to the service centre based on the surveyor’s report. It also argued that the commission did not have jurisdiction to entertain the complaint.Commission's finding on the car service centreThe bench comprising President Suresh Kumar Gupta and member Harshali Kaur found that Youwe and Cars had failed to properly repair the vehicle. It noted that the service centre had repeatedly reduced its estimate without explaining the reasons and had not obtained the complainant’s consent for replacing consumables and parts not covered by the policy.“The OP-1 was under a duty to check the engine and gearbox properly while repairing the car to see whether there is damage to these parts due to water logging or not,” the commission said.It noted that the gearbox problem appeared within a month of the car being returned after repairs. The commission held that the vehicle’s failure to run properly showed that the service centre had not carried out the repairs adequately.“The problem in gearbox within one month from the delivery of car after repair shows that car was not properly repaired. The non-repairing in a proper fashion tantamounts to deficiency in service on the part of OP-1,” the bench said.The commission also noted that the car remained with the service centre after it broke down, but the service centre had not produced a job card explaining why the vehicle was not moving. It held that the complainant’s evidence against the service centre had gone unrebutted.However, the commission found no evidence of a manufacturing defect that could make Nissan Motor India liable. It also accepted the insurer’s surveyor report, noting that the complainant had not produced material showing shortcomings in the assessment of the damage.What did the commission order?The commission, in its October 6, 2026, order, partly allowed the complaint and directed Youwe and Cars to:Repair the car free of cost and deliver it to the complainant.Pay Rs 50,000 as compensation for mental harassment, agony and litigation expenses.Comply with the order within 45 days of receiving it.If the service centre fails to comply within 45 days, it will have to pay interest at 6% per annum on the compensation and litigation expenses from the date of the order until payment. The complaint against Nissan Motor India and ICICI Lombard was not allowed.

articles.title: Shiva Sharma death case: Key Hazratganj cops shunted for failing to trace model Shraddha Dubey
articles.summary: LUCKNOW: Facing criticism over its failure to crack the mysterious death of 28-year-old restaurant owner Shiva Sharma and trace social media influencer
articles.body: LUCKNOW: Facing criticism over its failure to crack the mysterious death of 28-year-old restaurant owner Shiva Sharma and trace social media influencer and model Shraddha Dubey, the prime accused in the case, the Lucknow Police Commissionerate has removed the three key officers handling the investigation.The action comes amid mounting pressure on the police to arrest Dubey, who continues to evade arrest while making statements to the media despite multiple teams being deployed to trace her.The first to go was Hazratganj Station House Officer (SHO) Vikram Singh, who was sent to the police lines. This was followed by the removal of Deputy Commissioner of Police (DCP), Central Zone, Vikrant Vir, under whose jurisdiction the Hazratganj police station falls, and Assistant Commissioner of Police (ACP), Hazratganj, Rajneesh Kumar Verma.Senior police officials said the three officers were removed because they had failed to deliver results in the high-profile case, particularly in tracing Dubey and her associates. An entirely new team has now been put in place to investigate the case and secure the arrest of the accused.The reshuffle comes as questions mount over the police's inability to locate Dubey, her sister Rashmi Dubey and their driver, despite intelligence inputs suggesting that they may have crossed into Nepal.Police had earlier suspected that Dubey was in Mahimnagar, Nepal, and reportedly sent three teams across the border to pursue leads. An SUV registered in her name was also found abandoned near Rupaidiha, close to the India-Nepal border.Dubey surfaced publicly for the first time on Sunday in a video interview with a news agency from an undisclosed location. She denied involvement in Sharma's death and claimed that he had died by suicide after jumping from the fourth floor of a building near Balu Adda in Lucknow's Hazratganj area on October 9. She also questioned why CCTV footage from the premises had not been made public.Police have doubled the reward for information leading to Dubey's arrest from ₹25,000 to ₹50,000. However, her whereabouts remain officially unconfirmed, and investigators have not announced any breakthrough in tracing her.In the interview, Dubey claimed that Sharma was facing financial difficulties and had debts of ₹16–17 lakh. She also alleged that he had taken jewellery worth Rs 5–6 lakh from her residence and promised to return it. These claims have not been independently verified.Sharma's mother, Rachna Sharma, accused Dubey and others of being involved in her son's death. articles.summary: NEW DELHI: The BJP on Monday claimed that Congress MP and Lok Sabha leader of the opposition Rahul Gandhi has left for another foreign vacation,
articles.body: NEW DELHI: The BJP on Monday claimed that Congress MP and Lok Sabha leader of the opposition Rahul Gandhi has left for another foreign vacation, questioning whether he was travelling to meet his “chaos collaborators.”"RAHUL GANDHI IS BACK TO DOING WHAT HE DOES BEST: TAKING A BREAK AND ENJOYING A HOLIDAY! Rahul Gandhi is reportedly travelling abroad for a vacation. Rahul Gandhi is not in India!" Bhandari wrote on X."During Navratri, what is Rahul Gandhi doing abroad? Enjoying a break? Meeting his 'chaos collaborators'? A man who spends more time chilling than working-and then shouts, 'Vote Chori!'" he added.Bhandari shared a caricature of Rahul Gandhi depicting the Congress leader at a foreign destination, dressed in holiday attire and carrying a suitcase. The Hindi caption read: “Rahul Gandhi on a holiday again! As Rahul faced mounting heat with questions at home, he set off abroad for a change of air. Holiday mode on.”Rahul Gandhi has repeatedly faced criticism over his foreign trips, with critics claiming that several of these visits coincide with major protest movements in the country. They argue that the Raebareli MP should lead such protest movements and that his absence midway, if he is already involved, could disrupt their momentum. The BJP and its supporters, meanwhile, allege that he travels abroad to meet individuals seeking to oust the Narendra Modi government.Rahul Gandhi’s latest reported overseas visit comes amid protests in Delhi against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.The Congress-led opposition INDIA bloc has reportedly paused its demonstrations seeking Kumar's resignation, in view of the ongoing festive season. articles.title: Manipur violence: Protesters place bodies outside CM's bungalow after militant attack
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Protesters on Monday placed the bodies of two persons outside Manipur chief minister Y Khemchand Singh's bungalow in Imphal after they were
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Protesters on Monday placed the bodies of two persons outside Manipur chief minister Y Khemchand Singh's bungalow in Imphal after they were killed by suspected militants near the border of Imphal East and Kangpokpi districts.Angry locals brought the bodies to Imphal to protest the violence that has plagued the state since May 2023. They placed the bodies outside the main gate of the chief minister's residence in Babupara.It was not immediately known whether the CM was present at the residence during the protest.Police fired several rounds of tear gas shells to disperse the protesters, following which the bodies were taken to the Jawaharlal Nehru Institute of Medical Sciences (JNIMS). One of the injured, identified as Ksh Deven, was stated to be in serious condition, officials said.According to police officials, four others were also injured after suspected militants opened fire on a group of firewood collectors.Three persons are still missing following the incident, which took place at Khongbal Sunurok Uyok in Kangpokpi, a few metres from Nongshum village in Imphal East, they said.The deceased were identified as Arubam Ronil (35) and Lairenlakpam Inaobi (51). They were among 16 people who had gone to the hills near their village around 7 am to collect firewood when they were ambushed, officials said.Earlier on Sunday, at least 15 houses belonging to the Kuki community were torched in a hill village in Manipur's Kamjong district, forcing several civilians to flee to forest areas and a nearby Army camp.According to news agency PTI, a Kuki civilian was killed and four others sustained bullet injuries when suspected militants attacked the village.In a separate incident at Kamjong district headquarters on Saturday night, three Tangkhul Naga civilians sustained bullet injuries when rival armed groups belonging to another community attacked the village.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: A heart-shaped mourning pendant depicted in a 1635 painting resurfaced nearly 400 years later; it contains a tassel made from a dead child’s hair
articles.summary: A heart-shaped mourning pendant depicted in a 1635 painting has resurfaced nearly 400 years later, revealing a deeply personal story of grief from
articles.body: A heart-shaped mourning pendant depicted in a 1635 painting has resurfaced nearly 400 years later, revealing a deeply personal story of grief from 17th-century England. The jewel commemorates Robert Aston, the six-year-old son of English landowner Sir Thomas Aston, who died in 1634. It contains a tassel made from the boy’s blond hair and bears Latin inscriptions expressing his parents’ sorrow. The pendant appears in Sir Thomas Aston at the Deathbed of His Wife, a painting by artist John Souch now held by Manchester Art Gallery. Its modern owners possessed the jewel for decades without knowing its historical significance. They recognised it while visiting an exhibition featuring the painting and contacted historian and jewellery specialist Martyn Downer.The heart-shaped mourning pendant and the child behind itKnown as the Aston Deathes Hedde, the pendant is an example of memento mori jewellery, designed to remind people of death and the fleeting nature of life. It is heart-shaped and surrounded by a golden wreath. Black-and-white enamel decorates the piece, which features a skull motif and Latin inscriptions on both sides.The jewel was made to commemorate Robert, who died on May 4, 1634, aged six. A tassel containing a lock of his blond hair hangs beneath it. Such keepsakes allowed families to preserve a physical connection with loved ones who had died.The pendant’s inscriptions express the depth of the family’s loss. Its rediscovery has allowed specialists to examine details that cannot be fully deciphered from the small image in the painting.The 1635 painting that preserved the jewel’s imageThe pendant appears in Sir Thomas Aston at the Deathbed of His Wife, painted by Cheshire artist John Souch in 1635. The life-size portrait depicts Sir Thomas mourning his wife, Magdalen Aston, who died during childbirth that year.Sir Thomas stands beside their three-year-old son, Thomas. Magdalen lies in bed, while a covered cradle refers to the loss of their baby. The composition combines a family portrait with symbols of death, faith and the fragility of human life.The family had already suffered several bereavements. Robert, Elizabeth and Jane had died young before the painting was completed. Thomas, the child shown beside his father, died in 1636, just a year later.The painting is now held by Manchester Art Gallery. It offers historians a glimpse into the family’s losses and the ways grief was represented in early modern England.Latin inscription reveals the parents’ griefThe pendant carries Latin inscriptions expressing the anguish Robert’s death caused his parents. According to a translation of the text, it reads in part:“Your Robert died 4 May 1634 … In whom was our delight, through whom was our consolation, with whom the hope of his parents first perished.”The inscription describes Robert as a source of happiness and comfort for his parents. It also conveys how his death affected their hopes for the future.Although Souch depicted the pendant in the painting, its full inscriptions could not be read from the artwork alone. Examining the surviving jewel has helped reveal the meaning behind an object that scholars had previously seen only in painted form.How the long-lost pendant was rediscoveredThe pendant remained in the Aston family until it was sold in 1862. Its subsequent history was largely forgotten. The current owners acquired it around three decades before its significance came to light, unaware that it was the same jewel depicted in Souch’s painting.The discovery followed a visit to an exhibition featuring the portrait. The owners recognised the pendant in the artwork and contacted Martyn Downer, a historian and specialist dealer in historical jewellery and objects.Downer investigated the piece and identified its connection to the painting. The discovery also gave researchers an opportunity to compare the physical object with Souch’s depiction and examine its construction, decoration and inscriptions directly.Why the jewel is being compared with Shakespeare’s HamnetThe pendant has been described as a “Hamnet-era” mourning jewel because it dates from a period when child mortality and family bereavement were familiar features of life in England.William Shakespeare’s son Hamnet died in 1596 at the age of 11. Robert Aston died in 1634, nearly four decades later. Both stories concern parents who lost young children, but there is no evidence linking the Aston family or the pendant directly to Shakespeare.The comparison is historical rather than personal. It places the jewel within a broader period in which families used portraits, inscriptions and personal objects to remember the dead.The pendant demonstrates how mourning could be expressed through intimate possessions. Its lock of hair and inscription transformed a small piece of jewellery into a lasting memorial to a particular child.Pendant valued at £650,000Downer valued the jewel at £650,000, reflecting its rarity and historical significance. He announced plans to exhibit it at the Treasure House Fair at the Royal Hospital Chelsea in London from June 24 to 30, 2026. The fair has since concluded.As of October 19, 2026, Downer’s website continues to list the Aston Deathes Hedde among the objects available for sale. However, it remains unclear whether a sale has been agreed or whether the pendant has been reunited with the painting at Manchester Art Gallery.The jewel’s rediscovery has renewed interest in the portrait and the personal history behind it. The physical pendant provides a rare connection between a surviving historical object and the family tragedy recorded in a 17th-century work of art.Nearly four centuries after it was depicted, the Aston Deathes Hedde offers a tangible glimpse into how one family remembered a child whose death had profoundly affected them.You use AI every day. articles.summary: Two Indian-origin leaders have secured mayoral victories following the declaration of results in Canada's 2026 municipal elections in British Columbia.
articles.body: Two Indian-origin leaders have secured mayoral victories following the declaration of results in Canada's 2026 municipal elections in British Columbia.According to the news agency PTI, residents across the province voted on Saturday in local elections to choose mayors, municipal councillors, regional district directors and school board trustees. Elections were also held for park boards in Vancouver and Cultus Lake, as well as the Islands Trust.Harshan Ramadass wins Fernie mayoral raceIndia-born Harshan Ramadass defeated fellow councillor Kyle Hamilton to become the next mayor of Fernie.“We’ve done it, Fernie. Tonight you have sent a clear message that our community is ready to move forward,” Ramadass was quoted as saying by My East Kootenay Now.He secured 54.5 per cent of the vote, receiving 1,524 votes against Hamilton's 1,194.Ramadass said the result reflected the community's desire for collaboration, accountability and a focus on Fernie's interests. He expressed gratitude to voters for placing their trust in him and said he looked forward to working with the incoming council and residents to turn his vision into action.Surinderpal Rathor re-elected in Williams LakeIn Williams Lake, Indian-origin Surinderpal Rathor won re-election as mayor, securing a second consecutive term.Rathor received 2,116 votes, defeating his rival, Walt Cobb, by more than 1,000 votes. The Williams Lake Tribune quoted him as saying, “We won, we won!”He thanked residents for their continued confidence, as well as his wife, family and campaign team for their support. Rathor said he was honoured by the victory and committed to continuing his work for the community.Rathor had lost mayoral contests against Cobb in 2014 and 2018. articles.title: In 2018, scientists GPS-tagged 13 Burmese pythons but found that the devices recorded locations only 18.1% of the time
articles.summary: Imagine fitting a satellite-linked tracker to a giant constrictor and expecting a steady stream of locations.
articles.body: Imagine fitting a satellite-linked tracker to a giant constrictor and expecting a steady stream of locations. Scientists did exactly that with 13 Burmese pythons in Everglades National Park, and the results published in 2018 were both disappointing and encouraging. The devices recorded a position only 18.1 per cent of the time they tried, yet the data that did arrive was remarkably precise and far more frequent than older methods allowed. In wildlife management, snake research, or tracking technology, these findings explain what works, what fails, and what researchers recommend changing before the next attempt to follow these elusive snakes.How researchers fitted Burmese pythons with Global Positioning System tags in Everglades National ParkThe research team, made up of Brian Smith, Kristen Hart, Frank Mazzotti, Mathieu Basille, and Christina Romagosa, fitted 13 Burmese pythons with Global Positioning System tags inside Everglades National Park. According to the United States Geological Survey publication of their work in the journal Animal Biotelemetry, the team also placed seven additional tags on stationary platforms. Those fixed tags served as a benchmark, revealing whether habitat itself, rather than snake behaviour, interfered with signal reception. Every tag, whether on a python or a platform, was programmed to attempt a location fix every 90 minutes. The design mattered because large constricting snakes are top predators in their ecosystems and are often a management priority, whether their populations are threatened or invasive, yet nobody had proved this technology could deliver dependable data on them.Why an 18.1 per cent fix rate still gave 14.5 locations per python weekly, beating radio trackingHere is the headline number, the tags in this study secured a location fix only 18.1 per cent of the time they tried. At first glance, that sounds like a failure, because a tag programmed to check in every 90 minutes missed more than four out of five attempts. Yet the authors point out that the snakes still produced an average of 14.5 locations per animal per week. That is a large improvement over once-weekly tracking with very high-frequency radio signals, the established method for locating tagged snakes. In other words, a low success rate on each individual attempt still adds up to a far denser trail of movement than field crews could realistically gather in person, which is why the number is more nuanced than it first appears.Mean accuracy of 7.3 meters and mean precision of 12.9 meters, how reliable were python location dataWhen the tags did connect, the quality of the locations impressed the researchers. The authors reported a mean accuracy of 7.3 meters and a mean precision of 12.9 meters, which they judged to be very good overall. In plain terms, accuracy reflects how close a reading lands to the true position, and precision reflects how tightly the readings agree with one another. A very small share of readings were still flawed; 0.2 per cent of locations had a precision worse than one kilometre. For anyone building a movement map, those outliers can be screened out, but they are a reminder that every automated tracking record deserves a quality check before analysis begins. The takeaway is that the weakness of this technology was never about trusting the points that arrived; it was about how many points failed to arrive at all.Dense vegetation, underground hiding places, and underwater refuges limited satellite signalsWhy did so many attempts fail? The researchers found two explanations. First, dense vegetation reduced the fix rate, a pattern the stationary test platforms were designed to reveal. Second, they concluded that the pythons themselves also contributed to the shortfall, because the snakes spent time in microhabitats underground or underwater, places where satellite signals struggle to reach. This finding turns a technical limitation into a behavioural clue. A missing location is not always a failure of the equipment; sometimes it quietly tells you the animal was hidden below the surface or beneath water. For wildlife managers studying an invasive or threatened constrictor, that absence of data can be informative in its own right, provided scientists interpret it carefully rather than ignoring it.Tag failures and what the researchers recommend, pairing satellite tracking with radio telemetryThe study's most sobering result involved hardware. Half of the recovered pythons were either missing their tag or carried a tag that had malfunctioned, so no data could be retrieved from those animals. Even so, the authors concluded that Global Positioning System biologging remains a promising tool for obtaining frequent, accurate, and precise locations of large constricting snakes. They recommend that future studies pair the tags with frequent, very high-frequency radio locations, which would reduce bias and limit the damage when a tag fails. They also call for improvements to tag design to make such failures less common. For conservation teams, park managers, and anyone funding python research, the message is practical, adopt the technology, but keep a backup method running alongside it.You use AI every day. articles.title: China’s rice fields have a duck workforce: The birds help control weeds and pests as farmers grow rice and fish
articles.summary: Discover how China’s innovative rice-duck and rice-fish systems enhance crop yields and reduce pesticide use, creating sustainable farming practices that benefit both farmers and the environment.
articles.body: In rice-growing regions of southern China, a flooded paddy is often more than a place to grow a single crop. In many rice-duck systems, ducklings are put into the paddy during the early growth stage of the rice and, as a 1999 trial reported in Livestock Research for Rural Development describes, forage between the rows for insects, weeds, and snails. These are called rice-duck and rice-fish co-cultivation systems. The principle behind these systems is straightforward: animals can perform some of the functions traditionally served by herbicides, pesticides, and fertilizers in conventional farming. In many rice-duck systems, the ducks are removed before harvest, so the crop remains intact and farmers get both rice and ducks from one plot of land. Researchers have tested how well the idea works, and the results are less clear-cut than they first appear, especially for pest control by ducks.A 2022 field trial in northern Zhejiang tested ducks against weedsA research team led by Ping Qian published a detailed assessment in 2022 in Biocontrol Science and Technology, based on a suburban farming area in northern Zhejiang. The study, titled Effects of integrated rice-duck farming on weed pressure, herbivore-predator interactions and economic benefits, aimed to evaluate whether conventional farming could be replaced by a farming system with lower chemical pollution. It examined rice-duck farms alongside control and conventional farms in the suburban zone of northern Zhejiang Province during the rice-growing season. The analysis showed that the ducks kept weeds at bay within the paddies. Overall, organic rice-duck technology yielded an economic profit 7.6 times higher than conventional cultivation and 1.4 times higher than the control.Planthoppers increased, and spiders and dragonflies declined in the duck paddiesThe same trial made the story of pest management even more complex. Planthoppers and leafhoppers, both significant rice pests, were more numerous in duck paddies than in either the conventional or control fields. The predators, in particular spiders and dragonflies, were less numerous in the same paddies. The authors suggested that the decline in predators created an “enemy-free space” for herbivores, which may explain the rise in pests. The above-mentioned study found that rice-duck farming was less effective against major insect pests. Nevertheless, the authors suggested the method as a high-return organic farming approach for modern farmers.Qingtian’s carp paddies reflect more than 1,000 years of practiceFish-based systems have a long record in the same region. The FAO’s Agroecology Knowledge Hub states that rice-fish co-culture across southern China dates back more than 1,000 years, and it lists the Qingtian system in Zhejiang Province among FAO’s Globally Important Agricultural Heritage Systems. The hub refers to the system as one that produces rice grain and aquatic protein from the same body of water. It further says that the system efficiently uses the land by producing carbohydrates and animal protein simultaneously.A 2011 field survey found rice-fish paddies used 68 percent less pesticideThe Qingtian tradition was examined in depth in Ecological mechanisms underlying the sustainability of the agricultural heritage rice-fish coculture system, a 2011 paper by Xie and colleagues in the Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences. The authors describe a system that has persisted for more than 1,200 years, and in their field study the rice-fish plots yielded about the same as mono-cropped rice while using 68 percent less pesticide and 24 percent less chemical fertilizer. The study also found a reciprocal benefit: fish reduced rice pests, rice improved water quality for fish, and nitrogen use became more complementary.The field study done by the authors compared the rice-fish paddies to the rice monoculture and found that the yield and yield stability were the same for both systems. The authors also reported that yield stability matched that of rice monoculture, and that this complementarity in nitrogen use reduced nitrogen loss from the system.What the two studies suggest about sharing the paddy with animalsIn the Zhejiang trial, ducks suppressed weeds but did not control the main herbivore pests, while in the Qingtian field survey, rice-fish plots used substantially less pesticide and chemical fertilizer than rice monoculture, with similar yields. The two findings do not mean that every animal suits every paddy, since results depend on the animal, the pest, and the management practice. The income advantage in the duck trial applied only to paddies with organic certification.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: In 1983, South Korea’s planned two-hour TV search for war-split families drew endless calls, so the show kept running for 138 days, leading to 10,189 reunions
articles.summary: In 1983, KBS launched a groundbreaking 138-day live broadcast to reunite families divided by the Korean War, resulting in over 10,000 reunions. Discover the powerful impact of this historic program.
articles.body: Decades after the fighting in the Korean War ended under a 1953 armistice, many South Korean families still did not know whether relatives separated by the war and by the division of the peninsula were alive. In 1983, KBS, South Korea’s public broadcaster, launched a special live program to help separated families reconnect. It was a simple procedure. Relatives would come to the broadcasting station, fill out an application, and appear on television holding a sign telling their story, while viewers could recognize them by name or face and contact them. The organizers of the program could not foresee what the reaction would be, and what was supposed to be a short one turned into a marathon.KBS planned a two-hour special after a June 1983 morning segmentThe nomination form that South Korea’s Cultural Heritage Administration submitted to UNESCO records how the broadcast began. KBS titled the segment “I still haven’t found my family,” and it aired on June 21, 1983, on the morning program Studio 830, as the UNESCO nomination form records. While looking for guests, KBS staff saw how much separated families longed for reunion. The same form records that KBS President Lee Won-hong approved preparations for a two-hour special on June 23, 1983, that an advertisement inviting participants aired on June 26, and that KBS planned to feature 200 people but, after receiving more than 1,000 applications within two days, selected 850 cases for television.KBS extended the June 30, 1983 broadcast after an emergency meeting on its first nightThe nomination application also explains the events of the first night. The phones rang without a break, and applicants who could not get through to KBS took taxis to the station to apply in person. During the broadcast, an emergency meeting was held, and the show ran two hours and 15 minutes longer to air all the applications received, according to the nomination form records.The archive register entry lists 10,189 reunions from 100,952 applicantsThe entry for the archive on the website of the International Center for Documentary Heritage gives the final tally. In total, the nomination form records 100,952 applications for reunion, 53,536 cases aired, and 10,189 reunions. The project used 1,641 production personnel. The register entry says the archive holds 20,522 items, including 463 videotapes with 453 hours and 45 minutes of broadcasts, along with documents and photographs, and that it was inscribed in 2015. The nomination form also says the final broadcast took place at 4 a.m. on November 14, 1983.A Gallup Korea survey in October 1983 found 88.8 percent of respondents cried.The UNESCO Memory of the World nomination form for The Archives of the KBS Special Live Broadcast “Finding Dispersed Families” records that Gallup Korea conducted a random survey of 1,450 households across South Korea from October 10 to 20, 1983. Among the respondents, 53.9% watched the show until 1 a.m. and 88.8% cried while watching the show. The form adds that applications by phone still exceeded 60,000 per day, and that from the third day onward volunteers, from students to housewives, helped applicants.A 2020 academic study examined why the broadcast stood apart.Ju-A Joung’s paper,The Emotions of the Square and South Korean War Refugees: Study on the KBS Special Live Broadcast “Finding Dispersed Families” in 1983, published in the Korean Citation Index, discusses the broadcast in the context of war refugees and humanitarianism.Its keywords place the analysis within the context of war refugees, humanitarianism, and the UNESCO recognition of the archive, which suggests the author treats the program as both a media event and a record of displacement.The paper focuses on the broadcast’s scale, since it ran for 138 days, from June 30 to November 14, 1983, and drew large crowds to Yeouido Square. The author says the participants were largely wartime refugees, especially defectors from the North and children separated during the war, and discusses how the programme became linked with anti-communist propaganda and depictions of humanitarian reunion.The first South-North family reunions followed in September 1985The effects were felt outside the studios as well. In July of 1983, the president of the South Korean Red Cross called for speedy negotiations with the North’s Red Cross, and the nomination form states that President Chun Doo-hwan said in August that the problem could not be put off any longer. A North Korean delegation came to visit KBS in May 1985, and the first reunions of South and North families occurred in September. The form says that by 2014, there were 18,523 people who had been reunited with their families.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.
